coaching.headline: First Fangtooth was ours. Every one after that came within a minute of one of our deaths.
coaching.team: We drew first blood and took the first Fangtooth, then watched them take all four Fangtooth and Primal Fangtooth spawns after it and finish with ten structures to our four. Each of those Fangtooth takes came within a minute of at least one of our deaths. Countess and Belica brought the damage; Rampage and Argus kept collecting bodies.
coaching.lossReflection: When one of us is dead and their Fangtooth is close, give it up and hit something on the other side. After the first Fangtooth they took, we won a fight and took Mini Prime, the only won fight we turned into a prize. A conceded stack is cheaper than a stack plus more bodies, though it promises nothing.

matchup: Countess killed lane opponent Scarlett three times and died to her twice.
Rampage was the bigger match-wide threat: physical damage, growing Behemoth healing, and a share of their team kill lead.
build: A full ability-damage build; Megacosm and Tainted Scepter suit Rampage's health and regeneration.
eternal: This setup fits a Countess dealing most damage through spells.
The Tenth Seal is a draft alternative to Lich for Feast uptime, giving up the sustain that suits a melee mage.
augment: Sanguine Slash pays when Countess catches a lone target and adds nothing in a crowded brawl.
Shadow Strike is the draft alternative if Shadow Slip repositioning matters more, trading away the isolated-target bonus.
crest: Tempest damages nearby heroes and heals, suiting a Countess staying inside a fight alongside Blade Siphon.
improvement: Keep the damage package: Countess led our hero damage with three deaths.
Spellbreaker's magical armor does nothing against Scarlett's physical damage or Rampage's basic attacks.
If they end fights before Feast lands, compare a physical armor item, trading burst for surviving the first engage.

matchup: Argus punishes a mage standing still and got three kills on Belica.

build: Spellbreaker blocks one ability, a direct answer to Argus's stun orb.

eternal: A mana and economy setup that fits a spell-heavy mid.

augment: Combat Veteran is a scaling pick with no fight effect of its own.
Devastating Bombs is the draft alternative if Void Bomb lands on isolated targets, trading experience for burst.

crest: Soulbearer is the build's only active defensive item, so hold it for a Scarlett, Argus or Rampage engage.
improvement: Keep the damage package; its damage rate was far above this player's Belica baseline.

matchup: Feng Mao got the first two kills on Rampage, then Rampage killed Feng Mao three straight times and four in all.

build: The damage suits Rampage's health and armor, but nothing here adds armor against a physical-heavy enemy team.
eternal: Knell suits a duelist sticking to one target.

augment: Ichorous Glaive helps clears and rewards finishing low targets with Earth Shatter.

crest: Ortus rewards a jungler already getting takedowns, which this match rarely gave Feng Mao.
improvement: If Rampage keeps killing Feng Mao, compare a physical armor item over Sky Splitter, trading current-health damage for survival.

crest: Pacifier's dash is the build's only repositioning tool, so hold it for a Wraith or Rampage engage.

lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,274 hero damage a minute, more than 85% of Lt. Belica mid players this patch (28% of the team's). The damage came from Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Caustica.
Neural Disruptor at rank 3: 85s base, about 61.6s by the end (28% shorter) from 38 ability haste: Noxia 20, Spellbreaker 10, Soulbearer 8.
Lt. Belica dealt 52,232 hero damage, 28% of their team's, with +575 magical power from items.

Penetration: Combustion 9, Wraith Leggings 11, Caustica ignores 35%; against Wraith (level 18: about 53 magical armor, 15 after penetration; took 12,764 magical damage from heroes, 66% of all hero damage they took) and Argus (level 18: about 49 magical armor, 12 after penetration; took 13,943 magical damage from heroes, 65% of all hero damage they took) that is about 34% and 33% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Combustion (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 50 (+18%) Damage to the Target and nearby Enemies.
Wraith Leggings (item): Against Heroes below 40% Health: Abilities deal 12% bonus Magical Damage.
Caustica (item): On dealing Ability Damage to a Hero: While they are above 50% Health. For every point of Bonus Magical Armor they possess. Deal 0.2% more Damage.
Noxia (item): Deal 6% of Target's Maximum Health as bonus Damage.
Aion (Eternal): Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.

Sustain: Spellbreaker: Gain a Spell Shield that blocks the next Ability.; Soulbearer: Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.; 1,967 healing recorded.
Toughness: +40 magical armor; took 37,083 damage, mitigated 25,306, died 6 times.

Lesson: Lt. Belica's penetration cut through: Wraith took about 34% more magical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 18 their armor was about 53, about 15 after 20 flat + 35% penetration).

Loadout augment Combat Veteran: Generic: a little movement speed and passive XP that grows with level. Helps Belica reach max ability ranks, where her Innovation bonuses kick in, a bit sooner. (game text: Gain +2.5% Movement Speed. Passively gain +0.1-2 Experience each second. Increases with Hero Level.) Field: 53.5% in 2718 games, 32% of picks, above the hero-role's 51.3%.

Loadout Eternal Aion: Each spell cast builds mana regen and spell damage to heroes earns gold. Belica casts Void Bomb often, so this keeps her mana up and pays her for poking. (game text: Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.) Field: 49.2% in 691 games, 8% of picks, below the hero-role's 51.3%.

Loadout minor Bottomless Vial: Taking a river buff refills a potion and permanently adds a little magical power. A small sustain and scaling bonus, nothing Belica-specific. (game text: Killing a River Buff restores a Potion charge and grants +5 Magical Power permanently.) Field: 51.4% in 500 games, 72% of picks, level the hero-role's 51.3%.

Loadout minor Runic Focus: More magical power while your mana is high. Belica's Void Bomb refunds mana on hits, so landing bombs keeps the bonus up. (game text: Gain 0.2% increased Magical Power per 1% current Mana.) Field: 50.1% in 353 games, 51% of picks, below the hero-role's 51.3%.

Loadout crest Soulbearer: A shield, magical lifesteal and speed for 8s. Pop it before casting Void Bomb and Seismic Assault into a fight to heal off the burst. (game text: Anima:  Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.) Field: 53.3% in 705 games, 8% of picks, above the hero-role's 51.3%.

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 5 effects on one trigger: Caustica, Noxia, Spellbreaker, Soulbearer, Aion. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 4 effects on one trigger: Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Caustica, Noxia. Lt. Belica has 4 damaging abilities (Void Bomb, Seismic Assault, Void Drone hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 38 ability haste brought them back 28% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
The Eternal was part of it: Aion (Bottomless Vial + Runic Focus) sits on the same trigger as the items (kept alive in fights), so every extra second in a fight made them harder to kill.
Countered? 1 of the 3 players Lt. Belica killed built magical armor (Rampage). We killed Lt. Belica 6 times.
Copy it? Aion (Bottomless Vial + Runic Focus): 52.1% in 305 Lt. Belica midlane games, level with the hero's 51.3%. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.
